summary: Iteration 26 backend verification - both RT parser fixes confirmed working. parse_rt_file now correctly resolves quarter/year from snapshot_id parameter (no longer hardcoded Q1 2026), and DEFAULT_NICKNAME_MAP (31 entries) is layered on top of the explicit user-confirmed mappings (Trey/Treyana/Treyanna, Tad/Thad/Thaddeus, Keisha/Lakeisha, TK/Thomas, Ikey/Eric, Lennie/Glennice, Matt/Matthew, Starwars). Direct end-to-end upload tests against temp in_progress Q2 and Q1 snapshots all pass; nickname expansion correctly routes Trey/Treyanna/Treyana -> Treyanna Quick (3+ mentions), Tad/Thad -> Thaddeus Hashey, Keisha -> Lakeisha Martin, Ikey -> Eric Ostgarden, Matt -> Matthew Spath. /process correctly populates snap.employees[i].rt_mentions and review_tracker_bonus = min(mentions*0.5, 15) (capped at 15 verified for 32-mention case). 400 status guard on completed snapshot works, in_progress accepts. P0 sync-from-employees guard and nickname CRUD endpoint regressions also green. Production state cross-check: Q2 2026 employees_v2 has 30 records, 28 with rt_mentions>0 - matches main agent's report.
critical_code_review_comments: parse_rt_file (snapshot_routes.py:3101) now correctly threads snapshot_id through, prefers snapshot.employees for matching (so user's manual display_name edits propagate), and falls back to employees_v2 keyed by the snapshot's actual quarter/year. Logging includes (quarter, year, snapshot_id) for future debugging.

name_variations construction (line ~3178) places explicit user-confirmed mappings first (lakeisha/treyanna/thaddeus/thomas/eric/glennice/matthew/starwars) and then layers DEFAULT_NICKNAME_MAP entries on top via setdefault+append+order-preserving dedupe. Behavior is correct - explicit precedence is preserved while still picking up new defaults automatically.

First-name length>=3 dedupe filter (line ~3207) intentionally drops 2-char first names (e.g., 'TK') from matching - documented in agent context note. This is fine as 'TK' is mapped via DEFAULT_NICKNAME_MAP as nickname->Thomas, and the parser only iterates known POS first names so it would only fire if a POS employee had first_name='TK', which is the noise-prevention intent.

snapshot_routes.py is 3906 lines - file size is well above the 700-line guideline and continues to grow. Modularization (split CRUD vs upload vs scoring vs sync) is recommended whenever convenient, not blocking.

Minor: build of name_variations happens inside the per-row loop (line 3178) - it's identical for every row so it could be hoisted before the loop for a small perf win on large CSVs (710-row file). Not a correctness issue, informational only.
